idiom_name: override the copy hooks (initialize_copy / dup / clone) + a private factory class
implementation_notes: Every Ruby object inherits `Object#dup` and `#clone`, so non-copyability must be installed by hand: both methods funnel through the copy hooks (`initialize_dup`, `initialize_clone`, then `initialize_copy`), and overriding those hooks - or redefining `dup`/`clone` themselves - to raise `TypeError` is the realization. `freeze` does not help: `clone` preserves the frozen state while `dup` returns an unfrozen copy of a frozen object, so a frozen object can still be duplicated. Keep the constructor private (`private_class_method :new`) and expose a factory, and treat the guarantee as runtime-only - `Marshal.load`, `allocate`, reopening the class or a subclass can still create a second instance, so this stops accidental duplication rather than enforcing an invariant. The classic base-class mixin has no Ruby equivalent; a module that installs the raising hooks is the closest analogue.
code_sketch:
class FileHandle
  private_class_method :new            # factory only
  def self.open(path) = new(path)
  def initialize(path) = @io = File.open(path, "r")

  def initialize_copy(_other)          # dup and clone both pass through here
    raise TypeError, "FileHandle cannot be copied (a copy would double the descriptor)"
  end
end
pitfalls: `freeze` is not non-copyability: `dup` returns an unfrozen copy of a frozen object and `clone` returns a frozen copy, so frozen state says nothing about duplication.
Overriding `initialize_copy` covers `dup` and `clone`, but `Marshal.load(Marshal.dump(obj))`, `allocate` plus manual ivar assignment, and a reopening of the class still produce second instances.

Raising `TypeError` from a copy hook breaks library code that defensively duplicates arguments (memoisation helpers, `Struct`-style copying); the exception then appears inside framework code, far from the call site.
Subclasses and refinements can override the guard, so for a security-relevant handle keep instances behind the factory and expose only read operations.
